speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand what's going on, can you describe the skin lesions in detail and tell me exactly where on your wrist the pain is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the history of camping in Minnesota, preceding knee pain, and current wrist involvement, I suspect Lyme arthritis. Have you noticed any tick bites during your trip, or have you had any rashes like a bull's-eye lesion on your skin in the past few weeks?

REQUEST TEST: Lyme Disease Serology (ELISA and Western Blot)

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Lyme serology rules out that suspicion, so let's look closer at the current presentation. Can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions in detail, and have you had any recent sore throats or joint pains in other areas?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Those painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your hands and wrists are highly specific for secondary syphilis. Given your sexual activity, I need to confirm this.

REQUEST TEST: RPR or VDRL for Syphilis

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal syphilis serology is unexpected given the classic presentation, so I must consider other causes for these specific lesions and monoarticular arthritis. Have you had any recent upper respiratory infections, or do you recall any genital ulcers or discharge in the past few weeks?

REQUEST TEST: HIV Test, Hepatitis B and C Serology, and Joint Aspiration with Gram Stain and Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HIV: Negative; Hepatitis B and C Serology: Negative; Joint Aspiration Left Wrist: WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of Gram-negative diplococci in the joint fluid confirms gonococcal arthritis. I will now order a NAAT test for Neisseria gonorrhoeae from your throat, rectum, and urine to confirm the source. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
